title: The diffusion equation
spoken: The rate of change of the probability density with time equals D times its second derivative with respect to position.
explanation: Where the density curves upward it grows, and where it curves downward it falls, at a rate set by D. A peak therefore flattens and spreads.
assumptions: Independent steps with a symmetric step law and a finite mean square step.
Times long compared with one step, distances large compared with one step.
These are modern teaching equations in SI notation, not a transcription of the printed paper.

notes.title: Curvature in space
notes.explanation: The second derivative: how the slope of the density changes along x.

notes.title: D times the curvature
notes.explanation: The spreading rate: larger D, faster flattening.

notes.title: Rate of change in time
notes.explanation: How fast the density at one x changes.

notes.title: What it asserts
notes.explanation: The density changes in time exactly as fast as D times its curvature in space.

notes.title: Probability density
notes.explanation: Probability per metre of finding the particle at x after time t.

notes.title: Probability density
notes.explanation: Probability per metre of finding the particle at x after time t.

notes.title: Diffusion coefficient
notes.explanation: How fast the mean square displacement grows: half its rate of growth. Not a speed.

notes.title: Position
notes.explanation: The coordinate x along which the particles spread.

notes.title: Observation interval
notes.explanation: The time over which displacement is observed.
